the chromatin accessibility of the major Igf-1 promoter is tissue independent, but the accessibility of Stat5-binding domains, which are required to drive tissue-specific expression, is restricted to liver, independent of GH signaling.
chromatin accessibility of Igf 1 gene enhancers, but not promoters, is liver specific and independent of prior GH exposure.

chromatin accessibility at hepatic-specific Igf1 gene regulatory domains is established independent of growth hormone (GH) signaling, and that the major IGF1 promoter is constitutively accessible in liver, kidney, spleen, and human liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of gene regulation in the liver.
the regulation of the insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) gene.
the molecular mechanisms that control gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chromatin accessibility at Stat5-binding domains in the Igf1 gene is liver specific and independent of prior GH exposure.
the hepatic-specific accessibility of the IGF1 gene enhancers are independent of growth hormone (GH) signaling.
the hepatic IGF1 promoter is open and accessible to transcription factors in a constitutive manner, but the enhancers of the IGF1 gene are open and accessible to STAT5 only in the liver.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chromatin structure at the IGF-1 locus is established independent of growth hormone (GH), but is required for GH-stimulated IGF-1 gene transcription.
chromatin accessibility at enhancer elements is a tissue-specific feature, and this feature of enhancers is established independently of GH signaling.
chromatin accessibility of the major Igf-1 promoter is tissue independent, but that accessibility of enhancers is tissue specific.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chromatin accessibility is a key component of the epigenetic landscape that drives tissue-specific Igf1 gene expression.
chromatin accessibility of Igf-1 enhancers is independent from GH stimulation.
the tissue specificity of Igf1 expression is not due to tissue-specific regulation of the major Igf-1 promoter, but instead is due to tissue-specific accessibility of Stat5-binding enhancer domains.
